name: NINJA RF-cyber defeat (AFRL)
description: Air Force fixed-site RF-cyber C-sUAS. Software-defined radios intercept the drone-operator link and take control of or disable Group 1-2 UAS without the indiscriminate interference of broadband jamming; friendly drones can be whitelisted. NO PUBLIC DEFEAT RANGE: the 2 km ring is a representative planning figure.

maxAltitudeFt.condition: engagement altitude ceiling — Not published. null, never 0.

sectorDeg.condition: azimuth coverage: 360 deg. Manufacturer states "OMNIDIRECTIONAL ANTENNA SETS" and "All Ninja systems provide full 360 deg protection".
sectorDeg.source: Black River Systems, Ninja Gen2 product page

engageTimeS.condition: time from assignment to effect — Not published. 20 s is the app's existing representative for an RF-cyber takeover effect (lib-enforceair) and is deliberately longer than the 5 s used for broadband jamming, because a takeover must acquire, identify the protocol and then command the airframe. REPRESENTATIVE.
engageTimeS.source: No source; representative value consistent with lib-enforceair

pk.condition: probability the effect is produced — UNKNOWN. No public Pk. 0.6 is REPRESENTATIVE and set slightly below the broadband jammers because a protocol-specific effect only works on a supported airframe: AFRL's own framing is 'capable of taking control of OR disabling' commercially available drones, i.e. the effect is not uniform across the threat set.
pk.source: Unmanned Airspace, US Air Force expands counter UAS research
